May 7 WHEREAS the chief magistrate of the State of New-Hampshire at their Session at Concord, in the year 1798, assessed a tax of three cents, on each acre of land in the town of Stratford, (public rights excepted) for the purpose of making and repairing roads, and building bridges in said town. This is therefore to notify the proprietors, and land owners, in said town, that they have liberty to work out said tax any time between the first of June, next, and the fifteenth day of September following, by applying to us the committee, who are appointed to superintend and lay out said tax.
